args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; reverted to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The service was reverted to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The rollback tool returned 503 Service Unavailable and did not run after 4 retries, so v2.3.0 was redeployed through the deploy tool instead. Post-change status: v2.3.0 in all 3 regions, healthy, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure (the staging RC was already unhealthy before the production release) and check why the rollback tool is unavailable.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0 in all regions and passing health checks. SEV2 incident INC-0001 is open, and the on-call engineer has been paged.

- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. The failing v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an 18% error rate.
- **How it was reverted:** The `rollback` tool returned 503 Service Unavailable four times and didn't run. I redeployed v2.3.0 with the `deploy` tool instead. That version has been healthy in production before, so it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Current status:** v2.3.0 is live in all three regions, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the revert and the switch from `rollback` to `deploy`. It lists two follow-ups:
  - Find out why v2.3.1 failed. Its release candidate was already failing in staging before it went to production.
  - Find out why the rollback tool is unavailable.

content.text: The rollback tool is down: it returned 503 after 4 retries and did not run. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so redeploying it through `deploy` gives the same result and needs no approval.
